강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the fundamental principles of organometallic and coordination chemistry with a focus on their applications in catalysis and functional materials. We will examine the structure-reactivity relationships of transition metal complexes, covering both homogeneous and heterogeneous catalytic cycles relevant to industrial processes and green chemistry. Special attention is given to the design of catalysts for biomass conversion and the synthesis of functional polymers via coordination-insertion mechanisms. The course bridges theoretical concepts such as 18-electron rule, oxidative addition/reductive elimination, and ligand effects with practical examples in sustainable energy and material science.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to predict the stability and reactivity of organometallic complexes based on electronic and steric properties, design catalytic cycles for specific transformations including biomass valorization, and understand the mechanisms behind polymerization reactions. Students will also develop the ability to evaluate the efficiency and selectivity of metal-based catalysts in modern chemical synthesis.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 입문 - 무기금속화학의 현대적 관점과 촉매의 중요성
2 주차: 배위화합물의 구조와 결합 이론 (결정장 이론, 분자궤도함수 이론)
3 주차: 전이금속 착물의 전자구조와 반응성 (18 전자 규칙, 산화/환원 첨가 등 기본 반응 메커니즘)
4 주차: 리간드 설계의 원리와 입체전자 효과
5 주차: 균일계 촉매의 기초 - 수소화, 산화, 카르보닐화 반응
6 주차: 교대첨가 (Cross-coupling) 반응과 팔라듐 촉매 시스템
7 주차: 고분자 화학 입문 - 중합 메커니즘과 기능성 고분자의 설계
8 주차: 금속 촉매를 이용한 중합 반응 (Ziegler-Natta, Metallocene 촉매 등)
9 주차: 바이오매스 변환을 위한 촉매 설계 - 셀룰로오스 및 리그닌 분해 경로
10 주차: 지속 가능한 화학 공정과 균일계 촉매의 응용 사례
11 주차: 나노입자 기반 불균일 촉매와 균일계 촉매의 비교 연구
12 주차: 최신 연구 동향 - 탄소 중립을 위한 금속 촉매 기술
13 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 최종 평가

기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the ultrafast dynamics of biomolecules using time-resolved X-ray scattering techniques. We will cover the fundamental principles of X-ray photon interaction with matter, pulse generation in synchrotron and XFEL sources, and data analysis methods for extracting structural changes on femtosecond to millisecond timescales. Special emphasis is placed on interpreting scattering patterns to reconstruct reaction mechanisms and conformational transitions in proteins and nucleic acids.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design experiments for probing transient states in chemical reactions, analyze time-resolved scattering data to determine structural evolution, and propose mechanistic models for protein folding or ligand binding events based on dynamic structure factors. The course aims to bridge the gap between static structural biology and functional dynamics through advanced scattering physics.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 시간분해 산란의 물리적 기초 및 펄스 레이저/싱크로트론 원천
2 주차: X-선과 물질의 상호작용 및 산란 단면적 계산
3 주차: 동역학 실험 설계 및 시료 준비 (단백질 결정화 등)
4 주차: 데이터 수집 시스템 및 검출기 기술 (PIXEL, streak camera 등)
5 주차: 시간분해 산란 데이터 전처리 및 노이즈 제거 기법
6 주차: 구조 인과성 분석을 위한 역산란 이론 (Inverse Problem)
7 주차: 단백질 접힘 동역학 및 반응 좌표 매핑
8 주차: 리간드 결합 메커니즘 연구 사례 분석
9 주차: 펨토초 화학 및 광유도 반응 메커니즘 해석
10 주차: XFEL 기반 펌프-프로브 실험 원리 및 데이터 해석
11 주차: 다중 스케일 동역학 (fs-ms) 통합 모델링 기법
12 주차: 최신 연구 동향 및 학제적 협력 사례 (생물리학, 화학, 컴퓨터 시뮬레이션)

강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the chemical principles underlying protein structure, function, and dynamics. Utilizing concepts from biochemistry and physical chemistry, we will examine amino acid properties, peptide bond formation, secondary and tertiary structures, and the folding pathways of proteins. The curriculum integrates classical biochemical assays with modern biophysical techniques such as circular dichroism, fluorescence spectroscopy, and X-ray crystallography to analyze protein-ligand interactions and enzymatic mechanisms. Special attention is given to the intersection of chemistry and biology in understanding cellular processes.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to predict protein structural features based on amino acid sequences, interpret experimental data from biophysical methods to deduce folding states, and design simple experiments to investigate enzyme kinetics or ligand binding. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how chemical principles govern biological phenomena and prepare students for advanced research in biochemistry and chemical biology.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 단백질의 기본 개념 및 아미노산 화학 (Amino Acid Chemistry)
2 주차: 펩타이드 결합과 1 차 구조 (Primary Structure & Peptide Bonds)
3 주차: 2 차 구조 형성 원리 (Secondary Structure Formation)
4 주차: 3 차 구조와 단백질 접힘 (Tertiary Structure & Protein Folding)
5 주차: 4 차 구조 및 올리고머화 (Quaternary Structure & Oligomerization)
6 주차: 단백질 - 리간드 상호작용 및 결합 열역학 (Protein-Ligand Interactions & Thermodynamics)
7 주차: 효소 촉매 작용과 반응 메커니즘 (Enzyme Catalysis & Mechanisms)
8 주차: 단백질 변성 및 안정성 (Denaturation & Stability)
9 주차: 구조 결정 방법론: X 선 회절 및 NMR (Structure Determination: X-ray & NMR)
10 주차: 원자력 현미경과 전자현미경 활용 (AFM & Cryo-EM Applications)
11 주차: 단백질 공학의 기초 (Introduction to Protein Engineering)
12 주차: 최신 화학생물학 연구 동향 및 사례 (Recent Advances in Chemical Biology)
13 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 평가 (Final Project Presentation)

소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the design, synthesis, and functionalization of Metal-Organic Frameworks (MOFs) with a specific focus on environmental applications. Utilizing reticular chemistry principles, students will investigate the construction of porous coordination polymers for gas storage, separation, and catalysis. The curriculum bridges fundamental inorganic synthesis techniques with advanced characterization methods to address real-world challenges such as carbon capture, water purification, and heavy metal remediation.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design MOF structures tailored for specific environmental targets, optimize synthetic conditions for high crystallinity and stability, and interpret spectroscopic data to correlate structure with function. The course also aims to foster interdisciplinary thinking by integrating materials chemistry with environmental engineering concepts.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Porous Materials and Reticular Chemistry
2 주차: Fundamentals of MOF Synthesis (Solventothermal Methods)
3 주차: Post-Synthetic Modification Strategies for Functionalization
4 주차: Gas Adsorption and Separation Properties (CO2 Capture, H2 Storage)
5 주차: Water Purification Applications (Heavy Metal Removal, Organic Dye Degradation)
6 주차: MOF-based Catalysis for Environmental Remediation
7 주차: Stability and Degradation Mechanisms in Harsh Environments
8 주차: Advanced Characterization Techniques (PXRD, BET, XPS, SEM/TEM)
9 주차: Case Studies: From Lab Scale to Pilot Applications
10 주차: Emerging Trends: MOF Composites and Membranes
11 주차: Sustainability and Life-Cycle Assessment of MOF Materials
12 주차: Final Project Presentations and Course Review

detail.query: 유기화학, 유기금속화학, 촉매에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?

화 10:00-12:00(E7 - 315), 목 10:00-12:00(E7 - 315)
강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of organic chemistry and organometallic chemistry, focusing on transition metal-catalyzed reactions that form carbon-carbon and carbon-heteroatom bonds. We will examine fundamental concepts including oxidative addition, reductive elimination, migratory insertion, and beta-hydride elimination within the context of catalytic cycles. The curriculum covers modern cross-coupling reactions (e.g., Suzuki-Miyaura, Heck, Sonogashira), C-H activation strategies, and asymmetric catalysis using chiral ligands. Special attention is given to designing efficient catalysts for sustainable synthesis and understanding the mechanistic nuances that govern selectivity in organic transformations.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to predict reaction outcomes based on organometallic mechanisms, design synthetic routes utilizing transition metal catalysis, and evaluate the efficiency and sustainability of catalytic processes. Students will develop a deep understanding of how ligand structure influences catalyst activity and selectivity, enabling them to apply these principles to solve complex problems in organic synthesis and materials science.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 유기금속화학의 기초와 배위 결합 (Coordination Chemistry Basics)
2 주차: 산화첨가와 환원제거 반응 메커니즘 (Oxidative Addition & Reductive Elimination)
3 주차: 이동삽입과 베타-수소 제거 (Migratory Insertion & Beta-Hydride Elimination)
4 주차: 촉매 순환의 이해와 중금속 촉매 (Catalytic Cycles and Heavy Metals)
5 주차: 교차 결합 반응 I - Suzuki-Miyaura 및 Heck 반응 (Cross-Coupling I: Suzuki & Heck)
6 주차: 교차 결합 반응 II - Sonogashira 및 Negishi 반응 (Cross-Coupling II: Sonogashira & Negishi)
7 주차: C-H 활성화 전략과 직접 기능화 (C-H Activation and Direct Functionalization)
8 주차: 비대칭 촉매와 키랄 리간드의 설계 (Asymmetric Catalysis and Chiral Ligands)
9 주차: 금속 유기 프레임워크 (MOFs) 와 나노촉매 소개 (Introduction to MOFs and Nanocatalysts)
10 주차: 친환경 촉매 및 지속 가능한 합성 전략 (Green Catalysis and Sustainable Synthesis)
11 주차: 실제 산업 응용 사례 연구 (Industrial Case Studies)
12 주차: 종합 프로젝트 발표 및 최종 평가 (Final Project Presentation & Exam)

교과개요
This course explores the frontiers of ultrafast science, focusing on attosecond and femtosecond phenomena in matter. We will investigate the fundamental principles behind pump-probe spectroscopy and coherent control techniques to analyze carrier dynamics in semiconductors and nanostructures. The curriculum bridges quantum optics with condensed matter physics, providing essential tools for characterizing next-generation semiconductor materials and observing electron motion in real-time.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design ultrafast optical experiments, interpret transient absorption and photoemission spectra to extract carrier lifetimes and scattering rates, and apply advanced data analysis methods to characterize the electronic properties of emerging semiconductor devices. The course aims to cultivate expertise in time-resolved spectroscopy for solving complex problems in material science and photonics.
주차별 강의계획

교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to modern organic synthesis strategies, focusing on the design and execution of complex molecular architectures. The curriculum emphasizes catalytic methodologies, particularly asymmetric synthesis using chiral ligands and organocatalysts, as well as radical reactions for constructing C-C and C-heteroatom bonds under mild conditions. Students will explore the principles of green chemistry and sustainable catalysis while analyzing recent breakthroughs in total synthesis of natural products.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design synthetic routes utilizing transition metal and organocatalysts for enantioselective transformations, predict outcomes of radical-mediated reactions, and evaluate the efficiency and sustainability of catalytic cycles. The course aims to cultivate advanced problem-solving skills in constructing stereochemically defined molecules and communicating synthetic strategies effectively.
주차별 강의계획

This course explores the design and synthesis of advanced functional materials with a focus on metal-organic frameworks (MOFs), conductive polymers, and atmospheric water harvesting systems. Students will investigate the principles of supramolecular chemistry to construct porous structures capable of selective gas adsorption and moisture capture from air. The curriculum bridges fundamental concepts in coordination chemistry with practical applications in sustainable energy storage, catalysis, and environmental remediation, emphasizing the relationship between molecular structure and macroscopic material properties.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design metal-organic frameworks for specific gas separation tasks, synthesize conductive organic-inorganic hybrid materials, and evaluate the efficiency of atmospheric water harvesting devices under varying environmental conditions. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of how supramolecular interactions dictate material functionality and to foster innovation in next-generation sustainable materials.

교과개요
This course explores advanced strategies in asymmetric organic synthesis with a specific focus on the total synthesis of natural products and pharmaceutical agents. Utilizing modern catalytic methodologies (organocatalysis, transition-metal catalysis, and photoredox catalysis), students will learn to construct complex chiral architectures with high enantioselectivity and diastereoselectivity. The curriculum bridges fundamental mechanistic understanding with practical applications in drug discovery, examining landmark syntheses of bioactive molecules such as taxol, artemisinin, and various alkaloids.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design synthetic routes for chiral natural products using asymmetric induction principles, predict stereochemical outcomes of key reactions, and evaluate the efficiency and sustainability of modern catalytic systems in medicinal chemistry contexts. The course also aims to cultivate critical thinking regarding retrosynthetic analysis and the translation of laboratory-scale synthesis into scalable processes for pharmaceutical development.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 비대칭 합성의 기본 원리와 키랄 보조제/촉매의 이해

5 주차: Organocatalysis 기반의 비대칭 알돌, 마이클, 및 Mannich 반응

기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the design principles of biological systems and translates them into advanced polymer materials. We focus on biomimetic strategies for developing tissue-adhesive hydrogels, bio-friendly surface modifications, and rapid molecular diagnostic platforms. The curriculum integrates concepts from soft matter physics, surface chemistry, and microfluidics to engineer functional materials that interact seamlessly with living tissues. Students will investigate how natural adhesion mechanisms (e.g., mussel foot proteins) can be mimicked in synthetic hydrogels and how these materials enable point-of-care diagnostic devices.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design biomimetic polymer architectures for specific biological interfaces, synthesize or characterize tissue-adhesive hydrogels with controlled mechanical properties, and develop surface modification protocols that enhance biocompatibility. The course also aims to equip students with the skills to integrate these materials into simple molecular diagnostic systems for real-world applications.
학습윤리
Cheating and plagiarism are serious offenses and will not be tolerated. Any student caught plagiarizing or cheating will automatically fail the course. This also applies to students who knowingly allow their work to be copied.
교과정책 (방침)

4 주차: Bio-friendly Surface Modification Techniques - Plasma treatment, self-assembled monolayers (SAMs), and zwitterionic coatings
5 주차: Mechanical Properties of Soft Materials - Viscoelasticity, swelling behavior, and degradation kinetics
6 주차: Interface Engineering for Cell Adhesion and Regeneration - RGD peptides and topographical cues
7 주차: Microfluidics and Lab-on-a-Chip for Molecular Diagnostics - Design principles of diagnostic platforms
8 주차: Integration of Hydrogels into Diagnostic Devices - Sample preparation and detection mechanisms
9 주차: Advanced Surface Functionalization for Sensing - Aptamer immobilization and enzyme-based assays
10 주차: Case Studies in Point-of-Care Testing (POCT) - Development of rapid test strips and wearable sensors
11 주차: Characterization Techniques for Biomaterials - SEM, AFM, contact angle measurement, and rheology
12 주차: Sustainability and Biodegradability in Polymer Design - Green synthesis routes and environmental impact
13 주차: Project Presentations I - Proposal defense of biomimetic material design projects
14 주차: Project Presentations II - Final demonstration of hydrogel-based diagnostic prototypes

소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of first-principles quantum mechanics and machine learning techniques for studying complex many-body systems. We will review foundational concepts in statistical physics and density functional theory (DFT), then introduce neural network potentials, variational autoencoders for phase classification, and generative models for discovering new materials. The curriculum emphasizes deriving physical observables from first principles while leveraging data-driven methods to accelerate computational efficiency and uncover hidden patterns in high-dimensional quantum landscapes.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to formulate many-body Hamiltonians using symmetry principles, implement machine learning algorithms to approximate ground-state wavefunctions and potential energy surfaces, and critically evaluate the trade-offs between theoretical rigor and empirical accuracy in quantum material discovery. The course aims to equip students with the dual expertise required to bridge fundamental physics and modern AI-driven research methodologies.

기초학부
교과개요
This course introduces the principles of superconducting circuits for quantum computing and sensing applications. Utilizing Josephson junctions as nonlinear inductors, we explore the design and operation of qubits (transmon, fluxonium) and microwave resonators. The curriculum covers coherent control techniques, readout mechanisms, and noise characterization essential for high-fidelity quantum operations. Furthermore, we examine how these circuits function as ultra-sensitive sensors for magnetic fields, electric fields, and single photons, bridging the gap between fundamental quantum mechanics and practical device engineering.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to model superconducting circuit Hamiltonians, design pulse sequences for quantum gates, and analyze decoherence sources in open quantum systems. Students will also gain proficiency in interpreting experimental data from cryogenic setups and designing protocols for quantum sensing applications. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of the interplay between circuit topology, material properties, and quantum dynamics.
주차별 강의계획

교과개요
This course explores the ultrafast dynamics of strongly correlated quantum materials using advanced spectroscopic techniques, with a specific focus on time-resolved infrared (TRIR) and terahertz spectroscopy. We will investigate how electron-phonon coupling, charge density waves, and magnetic order evolve on femtosecond to picosecond timescales. The curriculum bridges the gap between fundamental many-body theory and experimental data analysis, enabling students to interpret spectral signatures of phase transitions and non-equilibrium phenomena in transition metal oxides and topological insulators.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design ultrafast pump-probe experiments, analyze time-domain spectroscopic data to extract relaxation timescales and coupling constants, and construct theoretical models describing the interplay between electronic correlations and lattice dynamics in complex quantum systems. The course aims to cultivate expertise in interpreting infrared spectral features as probes of symmetry breaking and charge transfer processes.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 강상관계 물질의 전자 구조 및 위상적 성질 개론 (Hubbard 모델, Mott 전이)

detail.query: Strongly Correlated Systems, Quantum Many-Body Physics, Quantum Monte Carlo Method에 관심이 있는데 어떤 과목을 들으면 좋을까?
detail.hyde:
양자 다체물리학개론 (PHY415-01)
학기

강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the physics of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. We will explore theoretical frameworks beyond mean-field approximations, focusing on emergent phenomena such as high-temperature superconductivity, Mott insulators, and topological phases. A significant portion is dedicated to numerical techniques, specifically Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) methods, including path integral formulations, stochastic series expansion, and the handling of the sign problem. Students will learn to bridge analytical field theory with large-scale computational simulations to analyze phase transitions and critical exponents in interacting fermion and boson systems.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to construct effective Hamiltonians for strongly correlated models (e.g., Hubbard model, Heisenberg model), apply advanced many-body perturbation theory, and implement basic Quantum Monte Carlo algorithms to investigate ground state properties and dynamical correlations. The course aims to cultivate the ability to interpret complex numerical data in the context of quantum phase transitions and to critically evaluate the limitations of current computational methods.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 강상관 다체계의 물리적 배경 및 평균장 이론의 한계 (Hubbard Model 소개)
2 주차: 양자 다체 문제의 수학적 기초 (Second Quantization 및 Green's Function)
3 주차: 경로적분 형식주의와 양자 몬테 카를로 (QMC) 방법론 개론
4 주차: Stochastic Series Expansion (SSE) 알고리즘 구현 원리
5 주차: Sign Problem 과 그 극복 전략 (Lefschetz Thimbles 등)
6 주차: 강상관 전자계에서의 위상적 질서 및 Topological Phases
7 주차: Mott 전이와 Hubbard Model 의 상전이 분석
8 주차: 양자 스핀 액체 (Quantum Spin Liquid) 와 Frustrated Magnetism
9 주차: 동역학적 상관관계 함수 계산 및 Spectral Function 해석
10 주차: QMC 시뮬레이션 결과의 통계적 오차 분석 및 스케일링 법칙 적용
11 주차: 강상관 시스템의 비평형 동역학 및 Tensor Network 방법론 소개
12 주차: 최신 연구 동향 (Quantum Computing for Many-Body Physics) 과 종합 토론

기초학부
교과개요
This course introduces the fundamental principles of quantum information theory and their applications to transport phenomena and computing architectures. We will explore how quantum coherence, entanglement, and superposition enable novel computational paradigms beyond classical limits. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks with practical engineering challenges in designing quantum devices for low-dissipation transport and scalable quantum processors. Students will analyze the interplay between quantum dynamics and environmental noise, examining protocols for error correction and fault-tolerant operations essential for real-world quantum engineering.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate quantum algorithms for solving complex transport problems, design basic quantum circuits utilizing qubit interactions, and evaluate the performance metrics of quantum devices under decoherence. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of the physical constraints in quantum hardware and equip students with the skills to innovate in the emerging fields of quantum computing and nanoscale transport engineering.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자정보의 기초 - 큐비트, 중첩, 얽힘 및 양자 게이트

4 주차: 양자 열역학과 에너지 전송의 양자적 한계

This course explores the quantum mechanical properties of condensed matter systems, focusing on superconductivity, magnetism, and topological phases. This course surveys modern perspectives on the fundamental constituents of matter and their interactions. Utilizing Quantum Field Theory (QFT) as a foundational framework, the course emphasizes practical results and conceptual understanding. While this is not a full QFT course, we will use its results to understand particle physics, meaning familiarity with classical mechanics and quantum mechanics is sufficient. Students will analyze the structure and content of the Standard Model, explore its cross-disciplinary connections to other fields of physics, and examine the theoretical motivations for pushing beyond its boundaries.

교과개요
This course explores the rich physics arising from quantum many-body interactions in low-dimensional systems, bridging condensed matter theory and advanced experimental techniques. We will cover fundamental concepts such as Landau Fermi liquid theory, BCS superconductivity, topological phases of matter, and fractional quantum Hall effects. Special emphasis is placed on scanning tunneling microscopy (STM) principles, surface electronic structure analysis, and the interpretation of local density of states to visualize quantum phenomena at the atomic scale.

By the end of the course, students will be able to derive key properties of low-dimensional materials using second quantization and Green's functions, analyze experimental STM data to reconstruct orbital symmetries and electronic band structures, and critically evaluate recent breakthroughs in topological insulators and quantum spin liquids. The course aims to cultivate a deep intuition for how dimensionality and strong correlations reshape the ground state of matter.

기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the theoretical foundations of condensed matter physics with a specific focus on non-equilibrium dynamics and first-principles computational methods. We will bridge the gap between abstract many-body theory and practical simulations, covering topics such as time-dependent density functional theory (TD-DFT), pump-probe spectroscopy modeling, and ultrafast relaxation processes in solids. The curriculum is designed for students interested in pushing beyond equilibrium thermodynamics to understand how materials respond to extreme external stimuli on femtosecond timescales.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to formulate non-equilibrium many-body problems using Green's functions and diagrammatic techniques, implement basic first-principles codes for electronic structure calculations, and interpret experimental data from ultrafast spectroscopy in terms of microscopic electron-phonon coupling. The course aims to equip students with the quantitative tools necessary to design materials for next-generation optoelectronic devices and high-speed switching applications.

1 주차: 고체물리에서의 비평형 현상 소개 및 열역학적 평형의 한계

교과개요
This course introduces the principles of quantum simulation using ultracold atoms and trapped ions, bridging the gap between condensed matter physics and quantum information science. Students will explore how neutral atom arrays and optical lattices emulate complex many-body Hamiltonians that are intractable for classical computers. The curriculum covers the preparation of degenerate Fermi gases and Bose-Einstein condensates, the implementation of quantum gates via Rydberg blockade interactions, and the design of variational quantum eigensolvers (VQE) for solving lattice models such as the Hubbard model. We will also discuss error mitigation strategies and the roadmap towards fault-tolerant quantum computing architectures.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate effective Hamiltonians for cold atom systems, design experimental protocols for state preparation and readout in neutral atom platforms, and implement basic quantum algorithms on simulated or real quantum hardware. The course aims to cultivate the ability to translate abstract many-body physics problems into executable quantum circuits and interpret simulation results in the context of phase transitions and topological order.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 시뮬레이션의 동기와 고전 컴퓨터의 한계 (Classical Limitations)

The curriculum covers 3D scene reconstruction from monocular video, social kinematics for analyzing human group dynamics in surveillance data, and generative AI techniques for creative content synthesis. Furthermore, students will develop the ability to analyze dynamic social behaviors using kinematic data and apply these insights to build embodied AI agents capable of interacting with real-world environments.

This course explores the intersection of Artificial Intelligence and physical laws, specifically focusing on Computer Vision and Multimodal learning for scientific discovery. We introduce Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs) to integrate differential equations into deep learning architectures, enabling models that respect conservation laws even with limited data. The curriculum covers multimodal fusion techniques combining visual imagery (MRI/CT), textual medical reports, and temporal dynamics to solve complex problems in Medical AI. Students will learn to build interpretable AI systems that not only predict outcomes but also provide physical insights into underlying mechanisms.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to formulate multimodal data fusion strategies for vision-language tasks, implement PINNs to solve partial differential equations relevant to biological systems, and develop robust medical imaging analysis pipelines that adhere to physical constraints. The course aims to cultivate expertise in creating next-generation AI models capable of generalizing across modalities while maintaining fidelity to real-world physics.

This course explores next-generation energy conversion technologies focusing on self-powered electronic devices. We delve into the physics of piezoelectric and triboelectric nanogenerators (TENGs), analyzing mechanisms for harvesting mechanical, thermal, and biological energy. Special emphasis is placed on bio-inspired biomolecular energy materials and their applications in wearable electronics and autonomous sensors. The curriculum bridges fundamental material science with device engineering to address challenges in sustainable energy harvesting.

By the end of this course, students will be able to design prototypes for self-powered devices utilizing piezoelectric and triboelectric effects, evaluate the performance of bio-inspired energy materials, and propose innovative applications for energy conversion technologies in emerging fields such as IoT and biomedical implants. 교과개요
This course introduces computational methods for materials science with a specific focus on machine learning (ML) and data-driven approaches. We will cover the fundamentals of statistical learning, neural networks, and graph neural networks (GNNs) applied to crystal structures and molecular dynamics. The curriculum bridges theoretical chemistry/physics with practical coding skills using Python libraries such as PyTorch and ASE. Students will learn to predict material properties (e.g., band gap, formation energy, electrochemical stability) from first-principles data or high-throughput databases, and analyze semiconductor/electrode materials for next-generation batteries and electronics.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to construct machine learning models to predict material properties with high accuracy, interpret the physical meaning behind learned features, and design workflows for automated materials discovery. The course aims to equip students with the ability to analyze complex datasets from semiconductor and electrochemical experiments, formulate predictive models for novel materials, and communicate computational results effectively to both scientific and engineering audiences.

교과개요
This course explores advanced solid-state chemistry and crystallography as foundational tools for developing next-generation batteries. We will focus on lithium, sodium, calcium, and magnesium ion systems, analyzing their structural evolution during electrochemical cycling using X-ray diffraction (XRD) and electron microscopy. The curriculum covers high-capacity electrode materials, solid electrolyte interfaces, and the thermodynamic stability of crystal lattices under extreme operating conditions. Students will learn to correlate atomic-scale structural changes with macroscopic battery performance, bridging the gap between fundamental chemistry and practical energy storage applications.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to interpret crystallographic data to predict phase transitions in multi-valent ion batteries, design stable solid electrolyte interfaces for dendrite suppression, and evaluate the viability of alternative metal-ion systems (Na, Ca, Mg) against current Li-ion technology. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of structure-property relationships essential for innovating high-energy-density all-solid-state batteries.
주차별 강의계획

This course explores advanced materials design and synthesis strategies for next-generation electrochemical energy conversion systems. This course explores the fundamental principles governing heterogeneous catalysis, focusing on the design and optimization of catalysts for clean fuel and chemical production. Special emphasis is placed on controlling micro-environments within porous materials (e.g., zeolites, MOFs) to enhance selectivity and stability. The curriculum bridges theoretical modeling (DFT calculations) with advanced characterization techniques (in-situ spectroscopy, microscopy) to elucidate complex catalytic cycles.

By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze reaction pathways on heterogeneous surfaces, design catalysts tailored for specific clean energy applications (e.g., hydrogenation, CO2 reduction), and interpret experimental data from surface-sensitive instruments to propose mechanistic models. The course aims to cultivate expertise in manipulating local catalytic environments to achieve high efficiency and sustainability in industrial processes.

This course explores the physical principles governing polymer systems, bridging the gap between microscopic molecular interactions and macroscopic material properties. We will cover statistical mechanics of long-chain molecules, thermodynamics of polymer solutions, and phase behavior in blends and copolymers. A significant portion is dedicated to computational methods, including Molecular Dynamics (MD) and Monte Carlo simulations for field-theoretic approaches, enabling students to model complex polymer architectures and predict material performance using AI-driven data analysis techniques.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to derive constitutive equations for viscoelastic fluids from first principles, interpret simulation trajectories to extract structural relaxation times, and design machine learning models to accelerate the discovery of novel polymer materials with targeted properties. The course aims to cultivate expertise in multiscale modeling and data science specifically tailored for soft matter physics.

By the end of this course, students will be able to elucidate the molecular mechanisms of olfactory reception and neural coding, analyze data from clinical studies linking olfactory dysfunction to cognitive decline, and propose innovative research frameworks for drug development targeting neurological disorders. This course explores the intersection of optical tools and neuronal circuitry, focusing on the development and application of fluorescent proteins for in vivo imaging. We will cover the biophysical principles underlying synaptic transmission, dendritic signal processing, and the mechanisms of learning and memory. Special emphasis is placed on utilizing advanced microscopy techniques to visualize calcium dynamics and protein trafficking at synapses, enabling students to design experiments that decode neural computation.

By the end of the course, students will be able to engineer or select appropriate fluorescent indicators for specific neuronal compartments, analyze complex dendritic integration patterns using computational models, and interpret electrophysiological data in the context of memory formation. The course aims to cultivate expertise in developing novel optical probes and understanding the cellular basis of cognitive functions.

교과개요
This course explores the developmental and evolutionary mechanisms underlying motor circuit formation in the vertebrate nervous system. Utilizing comparative neuroanatomy, genetic perturbation studies, and computational modeling, we will investigate how specific neuronal subtypes are specified, guided to their targets, and wired into functional circuits during embryogenesis. The curriculum bridges molecular signaling pathways (e.g., Wnt, Shh, Notch) with circuit-level properties, examining evolutionary transitions from simple reflex arcs to complex motor behaviors across species such as zebrafish, Drosophila, and mammals.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to trace the lineage of motor neurons, analyze the genetic and molecular logic governing axon pathfinding and synapse formation, and evaluate how evolutionary pressures have shaped the diversity of motor systems. Students will also gain proficiency in interpreting developmental data to propose hypotheses regarding circuit assembly rules.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 운동신경계 개요 및 발생학적 접근법 (Introduction to Motor System Development)

The curriculum bridges molecular biology with systems neuroscience to elucidate disease etiologies and develop potential therapeutic modulation strategies.

By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze the biophysical properties of ion channels and receptors using electrophysiological principles, interpret neuroimaging data in the context of synaptic plasticity, and formulate hypotheses regarding pathological mechanisms in neurological disorders. detail.hyde:
정신질환의 분자 및 신경회로 기전 연구, 뇌 - 신경회로 유전체 - 전사체 - 번역체 패턴 규명, 그리고 세포군 특이적 반응과 단일세포 전사체 이형성 등을 심도 있게 다룰 수 있는 가상의 강의계획서입니다.

정신질환 (우울증, PTSD) 의 분자 기전과 뇌 회로 연결성을 유전체학 (Genomics), 전사체학 (Transcriptomics), 번역체학 (Translatomics) 을 결합하여 단일세포 수준에서 분석하는 내용을 담았습니다.

강의실
소속
뇌과학전공
교과개요
This course explores the molecular and circuit-level mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders, with a specific focus on Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Utilizing cutting-edge multi-omics approaches, we will investigate how genomic variations, cell-type-specific transcriptomic responses, and translational dynamics shape neuronal circuit dysfunction. The curriculum integrates theoretical frameworks of neurogenetics with practical analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data to decipher cellular heterogeneity and transcriptional plasticity in the brain. Students will learn to map gene expression patterns across different neural populations to understand the etiology of mental illnesses at a systems biology level.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate hypotheses regarding the molecular basis of psychiatric conditions using multi-omics data integration. We aim to equip students with the skills to analyze single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify cell-type-specific gene signatures associated with depression and PTSD. Furthermore, the course seeks to foster a deep understanding of how translational regulation contributes to neuronal circuit remodeling and behavioral phenotypes, enabling students to design experiments that bridge genetic variation and neural circuit function.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: Introduction to Psychiatric Genomics & Multi-omics Integration (MDD/PTSD Overview)
2 주차: Fundamentals of Single-Cell Transcriptomics (scRNA-seq) Data Analysis
3 주차: Cell-Type-Specific Transcriptional Responses in the Prefrontal Cortex and Hippocampus
4 주차: Deciphering Cellular Heterogeneity and Transcriptional Plasticity in Stress Models
5 주차: Genomic Variants and Their Impact on Neuronal Circuit Dysfunction
6 주차: Translatomics (Ribo-seq) and Post-Transcriptional Regulation in Depression/PTSD

This course explores the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neurodegeneration, synaptic plasticity, and neural circuit formation. Special emphasis is placed on autophagy-mediated cell death pathways in hippocampal neural stem cells, microglial activation during neuroinflammation, and the regulatory networks governing adult hippocampal neurogenesis. We will also investigate the pathophysiological mechanisms linking chronic stress to cognitive decline, dementia, and depression, integrating recent findings from high-impact journals such as Nature Neuroscience and Cell Metabolism.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to critically analyze the signaling cascades involved in autophagy-dependent cell death and stem cell fate determination within the adult hippocampus. Students will gain a deep understanding of how microglial activation drives neuroinflammatory responses and contributes to psychiatric disorders. Furthermore, the course aims to equip students with the ability to design experiments targeting stress-induced mechanisms of dementia and depression, and to interpret complex data related to neural regeneration and synaptic remodeling.

This course explores the intersection of biology, physics, and computer science to decode complex biological systems. Topics include cryo-EM data processing, molecular dynamics simulations for conformational changes in auditory signaling proteins and neuronal ion channels, and visualization of pathogen invasion across the blood-brain barrier (BBB). The course emphasizes interpreting high-impact research from journals such as Nature and PNAS to bridge structural insights with physiological outcomes.
교과목표
By the end of the semester, students will be able to analyze 3D structures of membrane proteins to elucidate causes of sensorineural hearing loss, predict conformational changes in ion channels associated with epilepsy mechanisms, and visualize molecular interactions of bacterial pathogens penetrating the BBB. Students will also develop skills to critically evaluate structural biology literature and propose novel strategies for drug delivery optimization based on barrier modulation.

11 주차: Case Study Analysis: Decoding High-Impact Papers in Nature/PNAS on Membrane Proteins
12 주차: Future Directions: AI-driven Structure Prediction & Therapeutic Development

교과개요
This course explores the cutting-edge mechanisms of neural regeneration through the lens of epigenetics and omics technologies. We will investigate how epigenetic modifications regulate endogenous repair programs following neural injury, aiming to identify novel regenerative factors that can be harnessed for therapeutic applications. The curriculum integrates theoretical frameworks with practical analysis of high-throughput data (transcriptomics, proteomics, and epigenomics) to decode the control principles of regeneration programs. Special emphasis is placed on translating these insights into strategies for enhancing neural repair in paralysis and pain management contexts. Students will critically evaluate recent breakthroughs published in top-tier journals such as Cell, Neuron, PNAS, and EMBO J, and discuss the implications for developing next-generation regenerative biomaterials and international patentable technologies.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to: (1) elucidate the epigenetic regulatory networks governing neural regeneration and identify key candidate factors; (2) apply omics-based analytical methods to design and interpret experiments for controlling regeneration programs; (3) propose innovative strategies for amplifying neural repair effects to treat paralysis and neuropathic pain; (4) critically assess recent landmark publications in leading journals and understand the pathway from basic discovery to translational material development; and (5) formulate research proposals that align with global standards for high-impact publication and intellectual property protection.

The curriculum emphasizes understanding the biophysical basis of brain-computer interfaces (BCI) and developing novel applications for neuroprosthetics. This course explores the molecular mechanisms governing genomic stability and cellular response to replication stress. We will investigate how DNA damage is sensed, signaled, and repaired through homologous recombination and non-homologous end joining pathways. Special emphasis is placed on the interplay between protein-protein interactions in maintaining proteostasis and their critical roles in cancer development. Students will analyze how defects in these networks lead to genomic instability and explore therapeutic strategies targeting specific nodes in the DNA damage response (DDR) network for anti-cancer therapy.

By the end of this course, students should be able to elucidate the molecular basis of genome instability caused by replication stress, describe the intricate protein interaction networks involved in DNA repair and proteostasis, and critically evaluate current mechanisms of cancer progression driven by genomic defects. The course aims to equip students with a deep understanding of how targeting specific DDR components can lead to selective cytotoxicity in tumor cells while sparing normal tissues.

강의실
소속
생명과학부
교과개요
This course explores the molecular mechanisms underlying protein misfolding, aggregation, and structural degradation associated with aging. We will investigate how conformational changes in proteins lead to neurodegenerative diseases such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, focusing on amyloid formation and prion dynamics. The curriculum integrates structural biology techniques (X-ray crystallography, NMR, Cryo-EM) with computational modeling to analyze protein stability under stress conditions. Furthermore, we will discuss therapeutic strategies targeting protein homeostasis (proteostasis), including chaperone modulation, proteasome activation, and small molecule inhibitors designed to prevent pathological aggregation.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to elucidate the structural basis of age-related protein dysfunction, interpret experimental data regarding protein conformational transitions, and propose rational drug design strategies for diseases caused by protein misfolding. The course aims to cultivate a deep understanding of the link between protein structure dynamics and disease pathogenesis, enabling students to develop novel therapeutic approaches targeting specific structural motifs involved in pathological aggregation.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 단백질 접힘의 기본 원리와 노화 과정에서의 구조적 불안정성
2 주차: 단백질 변형 (Misfolding) 의 열역학 및 동역학 모델링
3 주차: 아밀로이드 섬유 형성 기전과 신경퇴행성 질환의 연관성
4 주차: 크라이오전자현미경 (Cryo-EM) 을 이용한 변형된 단백질 구조 해석
5 주차: 샤페론 시스템과 세포 내 단백질 항상성 (Proteostasis) 네트워크
6 주차: 노화 유도 단백질 응집체의 제거 기전 및 자가포식 (Autophagy) 조절
7 주차: 질병 유발 단백질의 구조적 표적 식별 및 약물 설계 전략
8 주차: 최신 단백질 치료제 개발 사례와 임상 적용 가능성 평가

소속
생명과학부
교과개요
This course explores the cutting-edge frontiers of stem cell biology with a specific focus on human pluripotent stem cells (hPSCs). We will delve into the mechanisms of direct reprogramming (transdifferentiation) to convert somatic cells directly into functional neurons or other cell types without passing through an intermediate pluripotent state. The curriculum integrates advanced disease modeling strategies, utilizing patient-derived iPSCs to simulate neurodegenerative disorders such as Alzheimer's and Parkinson's diseases in vitro. Furthermore, the course covers the critical steps in developing cell-based therapies, including genetic correction, safety validation, and scalable manufacturing protocols for clinical translation.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design experimental workflows for direct reprogramming of somatic cells into specific neuronal lineages relevant to brain disease research. Students will gain proficiency in establishing robust human pluripotent stem cell-derived disease models for high-throughput drug screening and toxicity testing. Additionally, the course aims to cultivate a comprehensive understanding of the regulatory and ethical frameworks governing the development of safe and effective cell therapy products.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 인간만능 줄기세포 (hPSC) 의 기초 및 직접분화법 (Direct Reprogramming) 원리
2 주차: 전구체 세포 (Progenitor Cells) 와 신경계 분화 경로 규명
3 주차: 뇌 질환 모델링을 위한 환자 유래 iPSC 기술 및 적용 사례
4 주차: 알츠하이머 및 파킨슨병 등 신경퇴행성 질환의 in vitro 재현 전략
5 주차: 세포치료제 개발을 위한 유전자 편집 (CRISPR) 및 안전성 검증 프로토콜
6 주차: 줄기세포 기반 약물 스크리닝 및 독성 평가 시스템 구축
7 주차: 임상 적용을 위한 배양 확장 기술 및 GMP 기준 준수 요건
8 주차: 윤리적 고려사항, 규제 승인 절차 및 미래 치료제 개발 동향

강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of aging biology, immunology, and gut microbiome dynamics. We will investigate how the immune system changes over time (immunosenescence) and how these changes interact with the composition and function of the gut microbiota. Special emphasis is placed on organoid models as a cutting-edge tool to study host-microbe interactions in an aged environment. Students will analyze mechanisms linking chronic inflammation, metabolic shifts, and microbial dysbiosis to age-related diseases, utilizing recent literature and experimental data from organoid cultures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to describe the molecular and cellular mechanisms of immunosenescence and their impact on gut barrier integrity. Students will evaluate how specific dietary interventions or probiotics modulate the microbiome to potentially delay aging phenotypes. Furthermore, they will gain proficiency in interpreting organoid-based assays to understand host-microbiome crosstalk and propose novel therapeutic strategies for age-related disorders.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 노화면역학의 개요 및 면역노화 (Immunosenescence) 개념 정립
2 주차: 장내 미생물군집 (Gut Microbiome) 과 노화의 상관관계 분석
3 주차: 장벽 기능 저하와 전신성 염증 (Inflammaging) 의 기전
4 주차: 오가노이드 (Organoid) 모델 시스템의 원리와 구축 방법론
5 주차: 노화된 오가노이드를 이용한 미생물 - 숙주 상호작용 연구 사례
6 주차: 대사 재프로그래밍과 미생물군집을 통한 노화 지연 전략
7 주차: 장내 미생물 이식 (FMT) 과 노화 관련 질환 치료 가능성 탐구
8 주차: 최신 논문 발표 및 오가노이드 기반 실험 설계 실습

강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the molecular mechanisms governing plant growth, development, and stress adaptation. Special emphasis is placed on the genetic regulation of cellular senescence in plants, focusing on leaf and root aging processes. We will investigate the signaling pathways triggered by abiotic stresses (drought, salinity, temperature) that modulate cell cycle progression and differentiation. The curriculum integrates classical plant physiology with modern molecular biology techniques to understand how stem cells maintain pluripotency versus committing to differentiation or senescence. Students will analyze the interplay between hormonal networks (auxin, cytokinin, ethylene) and transcriptional regulators in controlling these dynamic processes.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to elucidate the molecular basis of plant cell aging and stress responses, specifically identifying key genes and pathways that regulate stem cell maintenance and differentiation. Students will gain proficiency in interpreting data related to cell cycle dynamics under stress conditions and understand how genetic manipulation affects plant lifespan and resilience. The course aims to foster critical thinking regarding the evolutionary trade-offs between rapid growth and stress tolerance mediated by cellular senescence mechanisms.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 식물 노화 (Senescence) 의 정의 및 세포 수준에서의 노화 현상
2 주차: 식물 줄기세포 (Stem Cells) 의 특성 및 분열 메커니즘
3 주차: 줄기세포의 분화 결정 요인과 조직 형성 (Organogenesis)
4 주차: 스트레스 반응 신호 전달 경로 (ABA, ROS, Ca2+ 등) 와 노화 조절
5 주차: 호르몬 네트워크 (옥신, 사이토키닌, 에틸렌) 가 세포 주기 및 노화에 미치는 영향
6 주차: 전사 인자 (WRKY, NAC, DREB 등) 를 통한 스트레스 반응 유전자 발현 조절
7 주차: 엽록체 기능 저하와 광합성 관련 노화 기전
8 주차: 뿌리 줄기세포의 분열과 환경 스트레스에 대한 적응 전략
9 주차: 세포 사멸 (Apoptosis-like) 과 프로그램된 세포 죽음 (PCD) 의 분자 기전
10 주차: 식물의 수명 연장 및 내성 품종 개발을 위한 유전자 조작 사례 연구
11 주차: 줄기세포 노화 관련 주요 유전자 (e.g., SAG, SENescence-associated genes) 분석
12 주차: 스트레스 하에서의 줄기세포 유지와 분화의 균형 조절 기전
13 주차: 후성유전학적 조절 (DNA 메틸화, 히스톤 변형) 과 식물 노화

강의실
소속
생명과학부
교과개요
This course explores the molecular mechanisms governing protein homeostasis (proteostasis) and their dysregulation in disease states. We will delve into the ubiquitin-proteasome system (UPS), autophagy, and chaperone-mediated pathways that control protein degradation. Special emphasis is placed on Targeted Protein Degradation (TPD) strategies, including PROTACs and molecular glues, as innovative therapeutic approaches to eliminate disease-associated proteins. The curriculum bridges structural biology with drug discovery, focusing on identifying novel targets for treating neurodegenerative diseases, cancer, and metabolic disorders through precise modulation of protein turnover.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to elucidate the regulatory networks of protein stability and degradation, critically evaluate the mechanisms of ubiquitin ligases and proteasomal inhibitors, and design rational strategies for developing TPD-based therapeutics. Students will gain proficiency in analyzing structure-activity relationships (SAR) of degrader molecules and formulating hypotheses for new target identification in protein-related pathologies.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 단백질 항상성 (Proteostasis) 의 개념과 세포 내 단백질 품질 관리 시스템 개론
2 주차: 유비퀴틴 - 프로테오좀 시스템 (UPS) 의 분자적 메커니즘 및 조절 인자
3 주차: 자가포식 (Autophagy) 과 대안적 단백질 분해 경로
4 주차: 질병 관련 단백질 응집체와 알츠하이머, 파킨슨병에서의 단백질 항상성 붕괴
5 주차: 표적단백질분해 (TPD) 기술의 등장과 PROTAC 의 작용 원리
6 주차: Molecular Glues 와 다른 새로운 분해 유도 전략의 구조적 기초
7 주차: 신약 개발을 위한 타겟 단백질 발굴 방법론 및 가상 스크리닝 기법
8 주차: 임상 적용 사례 분석 - 암, 신경퇴행성 질환에서의 TPD 치료제 개발 현황
9 주차: 표적단백질분해제의 독성 평가와 선택성 확보 전략
10 주차: 실제 연구 사례 기반 프로젝트 발표 및 심화 토론 (신약 타겟물질 발굴 시뮬레이션)

교과개요
This course explores the behavioral ecology and evolutionary dynamics of wild birds, with a specific focus on their interactions with insects. We integrate classical field observation methods with modern optical technologies to analyze foraging strategies, migration patterns, and predator-prey relationships. The curriculum bridges ornithology, entomology, and optics, examining how visual systems and light properties influence avian behavior and ecological niches. Students will engage in data collection using high-speed cameras and spectral analysis tools to understand the mechanistic links between sensory ecology and evolutionary adaptation.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design field studies on bird-insect interactions, apply optical principles to interpret avian visual perception and communication signals, and construct quantitative models explaining behavioral evolution in changing environments. The course aims to foster interdisciplinary thinking by combining ecological theory with technological innovation in wildlife research.
주차별 강의계획

2 주차: Avian-Insect Interactions: Trophic Networks and Co-evolution

4 주차: Optical Technologies in Field Ornithology: High-Speed Imaging and LiDAR
5 주차: Foraging Behavior Analysis: Kinematics and Energy Budgets

13 주차: Field Project Presentation and Final Examination

교과개요
This course explores the intersection of chemical reaction engineering and systems biology, specifically focusing on the quantitative analysis of protein interaction networks. Students will learn to design and optimize chemical reactions for site-specific protein modification, a key technique in developing novel molecular tools. The curriculum integrates kinetic modeling of enzymatic cascades with network topology analysis to understand how local chemical perturbations propagate through complex biological systems. Practical sessions involve synthesizing functionalized probes and analyzing their impact on cellular signaling pathways using high-throughput screening data.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to construct mathematical models describing the dynamics of protein networks under various chemical stimuli, design synthetic chemical reactions for precise protein labeling or activation, and interpret large-scale omics data to identify critical nodes within biological networks. The course aims to cultivate expertise in developing next-generation molecular technologies that bridge the gap between synthetic chemistry and systems-level understanding of cellular function.
주차별 강의계획

교과개요
This course explores the molecular mechanisms underlying cellular aging and strategies for their modulation. We will focus on the structural and functional analysis of proteins involved in DNA replication, repair, and telomere maintenance. Utilizing advanced concepts from structural biology and biochemistry, students will investigate how protein conformational changes influence genomic stability and senescence pathways. The curriculum bridges fundamental molecular mechanisms with emerging therapeutic approaches to control aging processes.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to interpret the structure-function relationships of key proteins in DNA replication and repair systems, elucidate molecular triggers of cellular senescence, and propose rational strategies for targeting aging pathways. The course aims to cultivate critical thinking regarding the interplay between genomic integrity and organismal longevity.

2 주차: Overview of DNA Replication Machinery and Key Enzymes

This course explores the physical principles governing biological systems at the single-molecule level, bridging biophysics and molecular biology. We will cover super-resolution microscopy techniques (STED, PALM/STORM) to visualize cellular structures beyond the diffraction limit, focusing on phase separation mechanisms in cell organelles such as nucleoli and stress granules. The curriculum integrates CRISPR-based genome editing tools for constructing specific genetic reporters and manipulating protein interactions to study dynamic intracellular processes. Students will analyze how biomolecular condensates form via liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) and utilize single-molecule force spectroscopy to quantify mechanical properties of cellular components.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design experiments combining super-resolution imaging with CRISPR-Cas9 systems to investigate the role of intracellular phase separation in cellular function. Students will master the theoretical framework of polymer physics and thermodynamics applied to biomolecular condensates, interpret single-molecule data to extract kinetic parameters, and critically evaluate recent literature on the physical basis of cellular organization.

The curriculum also addresses viral oncogenesis, analyzing human endogenous retroviruses and exogenous viruses such as Epstein-Barr Virus (EBV) as drivers of tumorigenesis. This course explores advanced materials and device architectures for next-generation thin-film solar cells, with a specific focus on Copper Indium Gallium Selenide (CIGS), Copper Zinc Tin Sulfide (CZTS), and lightweight flexible tandem structures. We will investigate the fundamental physics of light absorption in direct bandgap semiconductors, defect engineering to minimize non-radiative recombination, and interface optimization for high-efficiency charge extraction. Special attention is given to the design principles of bifacial dual-junction tandems that push conversion efficiency beyond the Shockley-Queisser limit while maintaining mechanical flexibility for building-integrated photovoltaics (BIPV).
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze the electronic structure and optical properties of kesterite and chalcopyrite materials, formulate strategies for bandgap tuning in CIGS/CZTS absorbers, and design multi-junction tandem architectures that optimize current matching between sub-cells. Students will also gain practical skills in evaluating trade-offs between efficiency, stability, and mechanical flexibility required for commercializing ultra-high-efficiency thin-film solar modules.

교과개요
This course explores the fundamental principles governing thermoelectric energy conversion and magnetic materials at the nanoscale. We will investigate the interplay between electronic transport, lattice thermal conductivity, and Seebeck coefficient in nanostructured materials to optimize figure of merit (ZT). Special emphasis is placed on rare-earth based magnetic alloys for high-performance permanent magnets and their applications in next-generation cooling and power generation systems. The curriculum bridges condensed matter physics with materials engineering to address challenges in sustainable energy technologies.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to analyze thermoelectric transport phenomena using Boltzmann transport theory, design nanostructured architectures for phonon scattering while maintaining high electrical conductivity, and evaluate magnetic properties of rare-earth compounds for specific device applications. Students will also gain proficiency in characterizing material properties relevant to energy conversion efficiency and developing strategies for reducing reliance on critical raw materials.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 열전효과 기초 및 열전도 메커니즘 (음향자, 포논 산란)

교과개요
This course bridges the gap between raw sensor data acquisition and intelligent decision-making using Artificial Intelligence. We begin with advanced signal processing techniques for multi-modal sensors (LiDAR, IMU, cameras), focusing on noise reduction, feature extraction, and real-time filtering. The second half introduces deep learning architectures tailored for edge computing, covering convolutional neural networks for image recognition, recurrent networks for time-series sensor fusion, and lightweight model optimization for deployment on embedded systems. Students will implement end-to-end solutions that integrate heterogeneous sensor data with AI models to solve complex perception tasks.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design robust signal processing pipelines for diverse sensor inputs, formulate machine learning models for multi-sensor fusion, and deploy optimized AI algorithms on resource-constrained hardware. The course also aims to cultivate the ability to interpret model outputs in physical contexts and communicate technical findings effectively to both engineering and non-engineering stakeholders.

교과개요
This course explores the intersection of photochemistry, electrochemistry, and environmental engineering to address global energy and water challenges. We will investigate the fundamental mechanisms of photocatalysis for high-level oxidation processes in wastewater treatment and artificial photosynthesis for solar-driven hydrogen production. Special attention is given to the design and characterization of advanced semiconductor materials (e.g., TiO2, g-C3N4, perovskites) for efficient light harvesting and charge separation. The curriculum bridges theoretical concepts of band structure engineering with practical applications in sustainable energy conversion and pollution remediation.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to elucidate the reaction pathways involved in photocatalytic degradation of organic pollutants and water splitting reactions. Students will gain proficiency in selecting appropriate semiconductor materials for specific light absorption ranges and optimizing electrochemical interfaces for hydrogen evolution. Furthermore, the course aims to cultivate the ability to evaluate the stability, efficiency, and scalability of photo-electrochemical systems for real-world environmental applications.

This course introduces the fundamental principles and technologies of Bio-Micro Electro Mechanical Systems (BioMEMS) and microfluidics. Students will explore the design, fabrication, and integration of lab-on-a-chip devices for biological applications. Topics include fluid dynamics in microchannels, surface chemistry, cell culture on chips, 3D organoid modeling, and the development of wearable biosensors. The course bridges the gap between traditional MEMS engineering and biological sciences, focusing on practical device prototyping and system integration.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design microfluidic circuits for specific biological assays, understand the physical constraints of scaling down biological systems to chip size, and propose novel architectures for 3D tissue engineering and wearable health monitoring devices. Students will also gain proficiency in selecting appropriate materials and fabrication techniques (e.g., soft lithography, photolithography) for developing functional BioMEMS prototypes.

Utilizing femtosecond laser pulses, students will investigate phenomena such as harmonic generation, four-wave mixing, and coherent anti-Stokes Raman scattering (CARS). The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks with practical applications in label-free bio-imaging, super-resolution microscopy, and real-time monitoring of cellular dynamics. Emphasis is placed on understanding the physical mechanisms behind nonlinear interactions and designing optical setups for high-speed spectral analysis.

By the end of the course, students should be able to derive equations governing nonlinear polarization responses, design ultrafast laser systems for specific spectroscopic applications, and interpret complex imaging data from biological samples without exogenous labels. The course aims to cultivate expertise in developing novel optical probes for deep-tissue imaging and analyzing transient molecular processes on femtosecond timescales.

교과개요
This course explores the neural mechanisms underlying motor control and behavior through computational modeling and non-invasive neuromodulation techniques. We will integrate principles from computational neurophysiology to decode how the brain generates, plans, and executes movements. Special emphasis is placed on understanding sensorimotor integration, motor learning dynamics, and the application of transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS) and transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) as tools for probing and modulating cortical circuits. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks with practical data analysis using open-source neurophysiological datasets.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to construct computational models of motor pathways, analyze neural signals related to movement execution and learning, and design experiments utilizing non-invasive neuromodulation to test hypotheses about motor control. The course aims to foster a deep understanding of how quantitative methods can elucidate the biological basis of voluntary action and plasticity in the motor cortex.

This course explores the intersection of neuroscience, human-computer interaction (HCI), and autonomous mobility systems. We investigate how neural signals can be decoded to control mobile platforms and how haptic feedback loops can modulate user behavior in dynamic environments. Topics include brain-computer interface (BCI) architectures, neurofeedback mechanisms for motor skill acquisition, neuromodulation techniques for attention regulation, and the design of safe human-robot collaboration protocols. The curriculum bridges theoretical neuroscience with practical engineering applications in smart mobility.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design BCI-based control systems for mobile devices, interpret neural data to infer cognitive states relevant to driving or navigation tasks, and implement neuromodulatory strategies to enhance human-vehicle interaction safety. Students will also develop proficiency in integrating haptic feedback with visual interfaces to create immersive neuro-mobility experiences.

교과개요
This course explores the theoretical foundations of learning over networks, bridging information theory and machine learning. We examine how agents exchange information to learn collectively, focusing on distributed optimization, consensus algorithms, and the convergence properties of decentralized learning systems. The curriculum integrates core concepts from information theory—such as entropy, mutual information, and channel capacity—with modern deep learning architectures to analyze the efficiency and robustness of networked learning. Students will investigate the trade-offs between communication cost and model accuracy, and explore recent advances in federated learning and over-the-air computation.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate distributed learning problems using information-theoretic metrics, derive convergence rates for various network topologies under different communication constraints, and design efficient protocols for collaborative model training across heterogeneous devices. The course aims to equip students with the mathematical tools necessary to analyze the scalability and privacy guarantees of large-scale machine learning systems operating over networks.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 정보이론의 기초 (엔트로피, 상호정보량, 채널 용량) 및 분산 학습 개요

6 주차: 공중 계산 (Over-the-Air Computation) 과 무선 네트워크에서의 머신러닝
7 주차: 이질적인 데이터와 모델 불일치 (Heterogeneity) 를 고려한 알고리즘 설계

The curriculum covers Trustworthy AI principles, including robustness against adversarial attacks, fairness auditing, and explainability techniques essential for deploying AI in critical domains. Furthermore, we delve into On-device AI optimization strategies for edge computing constraints and Multi-modal AI frameworks that fuse heterogeneous data sources (text, image, audio) to enhance reasoning capabilities. Students will analyze mechanisms linking chronic inflammation, metabolic shifts, and microbial dysbiosis to age-related diseases, utilizing recent literature and experimental data from organoid cultures.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to describe the molecular and cellular mechanisms of immunosenescence and their impact on gut barrier integrity. Students will evaluate how specific dietary interventions or probiotics modulate the microbiome to potentially delay aging phenotypes. Furthermore, they will gain proficiency in interpreting organoid-based assays to understand host-microbiome crosstalk and propose novel therapeutic strategies for age-related disorders.

This course explores the molecular and circuit-level mechanisms underlying psychiatric disorders, with a specific focus on Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) and Post-Traumatic Stress Disorder (PTSD). Utilizing cutting-edge multi-omics approaches, we will investigate how genomic variations, cell-type-specific transcriptomic responses, and translational dynamics shape neuronal circuit dysfunction. The curriculum integrates theoretical frameworks of neurogenetics with practical analysis of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) data to decipher cellular heterogeneity and transcriptional plasticity in the brain. Students will learn to map gene expression patterns across different neural populations to understand the etiology of mental illnesses at a systems biology level.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate hypotheses regarding the molecular basis of psychiatric conditions using multi-omics data integration. We aim to equip students with the skills to analyze single-cell transcriptomic datasets to identify cell-type-specific gene signatures associated with depression and PTSD. Furthermore, the course seeks to foster a deep understanding of how translational regulation contributes to neuronal circuit remodeling and behavioral phenotypes, enabling students to design experiments that bridge genetic variation and neural circuit function.

This course explores advanced imaging modalities and therapeutic technologies at the intersection of ultrasound, photoacoustic imaging, and nanomedicine. We will cover the physical principles behind medical imaging, signal processing techniques for high-resolution reconstruction, and machine learning algorithms for automated diagnosis and image enhancement. Special emphasis is placed on developing nano-diagnostic/therapeutic platforms that integrate multimodal imaging with targeted therapy. Students will learn to design experiments combining optical and acoustic waves for deep tissue visualization and therapeutic monitoring.

By the end of this course, students should be able to formulate inverse problems in medical imaging using statistical signal processing, apply deep learning models to improve image quality and diagnostic accuracy, and design nanoscale platforms for targeted drug delivery and real-time therapy monitoring. The course aims to foster interdisciplinary skills bridging physics, engineering, and data science to solve complex challenges in precision medicine.

This course explores the interdisciplinary field of robotics, integrating mechanics, electronics, control theory, and artificial intelligence. By the end of this course, students will be able to design mechatronic systems that mimic natural movement patterns, select and integrate appropriate sensors and actuators for specific industrial or defense applications, and implement robust control strategies for dynamic environments. This course explores the design principles and implementation strategies for integrated circuits tailored to biomedical and energy management applications. By the end of this course, students will be able to design low-power analog circuits suitable for wearable biomedical sensors, optimize power consumption in sensor nodes, and develop control logic for Li-ion battery monitoring systems. 교과개요
This course explores the intersection of quantum optics, biomedical imaging, and complex systems analysis. We will investigate advanced optical techniques including Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy (DOS) and Tomography for deep tissue characterization, as well as Speckle Contrast Imaging for non-invasive blood flow monitoring. The curriculum integrates these optical methods with the complexity theory of biosignals to analyze physiological dynamics. Furthermore, we will examine the theoretical underpinnings of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnostics through modern physics lenses, specifically focusing on microcirculation studies and acoustic resonance in biological tissues. Finally, the course covers Quantum Optics principles applied to low-light sensing and Sound/Music Visualization algorithms for interpreting complex bio-acoustic data.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design optical setups for diffuse spectroscopy and speckle contrast flowmetry, apply complexity metrics (e.g., fractal dimension, entropy) to biosignals such as heart rate variability and blood flow fluctuations, and critically evaluate the physical basis of TCM diagnostic methods like pulse diagnosis. Students will also develop skills in visualizing sound and music data to extract meaningful patterns from noisy biological environments, ultimately bridging quantum optical theory with practical biomedical applications.

This course explores advanced principles and applications of Biomedical Optics, focusing on interferometric microscopy techniques and wavelength-swept laser systems. Students will delve into the theoretical foundations of Fourier-domain image processing to analyze optical coherence tomography (OCT) signals and reconstruct high-resolution 3D images of biological tissues. The curriculum bridges wave optics, signal processing, and biomedical engineering to enable the design and analysis of next-generation diagnostic imaging devices.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to model light-matter interactions in biological media, design interferometric setups using tunable laser sources, and implement Fourier-domain algorithms for noise reduction and image enhancement. The course aims to cultivate expertise in translating optical physics concepts into practical solutions for deep-tissue imaging and functional analysis.

교과개요
This course provides a comprehensive overview of the molecular and cellular mechanisms underlying neurodegenerative diseases, with a specific focus on aging-related neuronal decline. Utilizing insights from recent breakthroughs in proteostasis, mitochondrial dysfunction, and synaptic plasticity, we will explore the pathological hallmarks of Alzheimer's disease, Parkinson's disease, and other dementias. The curriculum bridges basic neuroscience research with clinical implications, examining how lifestyle factors and genetic predispositions accelerate or mitigate neurodegeneration. Students will analyze current therapeutic strategies, including immunotherapy, gene editing, and regenerative medicine, while critically evaluating the challenges in translating preclinical findings to human trials.
교과목표
By the end of the semester, students should be able to elucidate the pathophysiological pathways leading to neuronal loss and cognitive impairment, interpret key biomarkers used in disease diagnosis and progression monitoring, and design experimental approaches to target specific mechanisms of neurodegeneration. The course also aims to foster a deep understanding of the intersection between aging biology and neurological health, preparing students for advanced research or clinical practice in neurology.

Additionally, the course aims to equip students with skills to engineer scalable fabrication processes for bio-FETs and integrate biomolecular control technologies into functional nano/micro-systems.

The curriculum integrates classical biochemistry with modern systems biology approaches to analyze how dysregulation in these pathways leads to chronic metabolic diseases.

By the end of this course, students will be able to map complex signaling cascades involved in glucose and lipid metabolism, critically evaluate the role of cellular stress sensors in disease progression, and design experiments to probe the interplay between metabolic flux and signal transduction. This course explores the physical principles governing biological systems at the single-molecule level, bridging biophysics and molecular biology. We will cover super-resolution microscopy techniques (STED, PALM/STORM) to visualize cellular structures beyond the diffraction limit, focusing on phase separation mechanisms in cell organelles such as nucleoli and stress granules. The curriculum integrates CRISPR-based genome editing tools for constructing specific genetic reporters and manipulating protein interactions to study dynamic intracellular processes. Students will analyze how biomolecular condensates form via liquid-liquid phase separation (LLPS) and utilize single-molecule force spectroscopy to quantify mechanical properties of cellular components.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students should be able to design experiments combining super-resolution imaging with CRISPR-Cas9 systems to investigate the role of intracellular phase separation in cellular function. Students will master the theoretical framework of polymer physics and thermodynamics applied to biomolecular condensates, interpret single-molecule data to extract kinetic parameters, and critically evaluate recent literature on the physical basis of cellular organization.

This course explores the frontiers of quantum optics with a specific focus on non-linear light-matter interactions and ultrafast dynamics. We will investigate how strong laser fields induce non-linear optical phenomena such as high-harmonic generation, attosecond pulse production, and the formation of macroscopic quantum states like Rydberg polaritons. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks including time-dependent perturbation theory, density matrix formalism, and semi-classical models to explain complex transient behaviors in condensed matter and atomic systems. Special attention is given to analyzing strong-field correlations and the breakdown of perturbative regimes.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to model non-linear optical responses in various media, design experiments for probing ultrafast electron and nuclear dynamics, and interpret spectroscopic data involving high-order harmonic generation. Students will gain deep insights into the interplay between strong-field ionization and many-body correlations, enabling them to propose novel schemes for generating coherent XUV/X-ray sources and controlling quantum states on attosecond timescales.
주차별 강의계획

2 주차: 강한 레이저장에서의 원자 상호작용 및 고조파 생성 (High-Harmonic Generation theory)
3 주차: 밀도 행렬 형식과 초고속 동역학 모델링 (Density Matrix & Ultrafast Dynamics)
4 주차: 리드베리 폴라리톤과 거시적 양자 상태 형성 (Rydberg Polaritons & Macroscopic Quantum States)
5 주차: 비선형 광원 설계 및 실험 기법 (Non-linear Light Source Design & Techniques)
6 주차: 강상관계 시스템에서의 양자 상관성 분석 (Quantum Correlations in Strongly Correlated Systems)
7 주차: 펨토초/아토초 분광학 데이터 해석 사례 연구 (Case Studies in Femto/Attosecond Spectroscopy)
