This course provides a comprehensive introduction to the theory and computational methods of strongly correlated quantum many-body systems. We will explore fundamental concepts such as Fermi liquids, Mott insulators, high-temperature superconductivity, and topological phases of matter. A significant portion of the curriculum is dedicated to numerical techniques, with a special emphasis on the Quantum Monte Carlo (QMC) method for solving lattice models like the Hubbard model. Students will learn how to handle sign problems, implement stochastic series expansion, and analyze large-scale simulation data to extract physical observables.

By the end of the course, students should be able to formulate Hamiltonians for interacting many-body systems, apply mean-field theory and renormalization group concepts qualitatively, and perform basic Quantum Monte Carlo simulations using modern algorithms. This course explores the intersection of modern cryptography, quantum computing, and artificial intelligence. We will cover classical public-key cryptosystems and their vulnerabilities to quantum attacks, introducing post-quantum cryptographic standards (NIST PQC). The curriculum integrates AI security principles, focusing on adversarial machine learning, model inversion attacks, and privacy-preserving computation techniques such as Differential Privacy and Secure Multi-Party Computation. Special attention is given to Vehicular Security architectures, including V2X communication protocols, key management in autonomous driving systems, and defense against spoofing or jamming attacks in smart transportation networks.

By the end of this course, students will be able to design quantum-resistant cryptographic schemes for next-generation secure communications, evaluate AI models against privacy threats and adversarial perturbations, and implement security protocols for vehicular ad-hoc networks (VANETs). Students will gain practical skills in applying Privacy Enhancing Technologies (PETs) to real-world data scenarios and understanding the theoretical foundations required to secure systems against both classical and quantum computational threats.

This course explores the intersection of condensed matter physics, quantum mechanics, and information theory. We will investigate how quantum coherence and entanglement manifest in mesoscopic systems, focusing on electron transport through nanostructures such as quantum dots and nanowires. The curriculum bridges fundamental concepts like Landauer-Büttiker formalism with emerging applications in quantum computing architectures, including superconducting qubits and topological states. Students will analyze non-equilibrium dynamics, decoherence mechanisms, and the design principles for scalable quantum devices.

By the end of this course, students should be able to derive transport equations for mesoscopic systems, interpret experimental data from scanning tunneling microscopy and quantum point contact measurements, and formulate basic models for qubit control and error correction. This course explores the intersection of quantum optics, biomedical imaging, and complex systems analysis. We will investigate advanced optical techniques including Diffuse Optical Spectroscopy (DOS) and Tomography for deep tissue characterization, as well as Speckle Contrast Imaging for non-invasive blood flow monitoring. The curriculum integrates these optical methods with the complexity theory of biosignals to analyze physiological dynamics. Furthermore, we will examine the theoretical underpinnings of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) diagnostics through modern physics lenses, specifically focusing on microcirculation studies and acoustic resonance in biological tissues. Finally, the course covers Quantum Optics principles applied to low-light sensing and Sound/Music Visualization algorithms for interpreting complex bio-acoustic data.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to design optical setups for diffuse spectroscopy and speckle contrast flowmetry, apply complexity metrics (e.g., fractal dimension, entropy) to biosignals such as heart rate variability and blood flow fluctuations, and critically evaluate the physical basis of TCM diagnostic methods like pulse diagnosis. Students will also develop skills in visualizing sound and music data to extract meaningful patterns from noisy biological environments, ultimately bridging quantum optical theory with practical biomedical applications.

기초학부
교과개요
This course explores the intersection of quantum optics and advanced imaging techniques, focusing on the development of super-resolution microscopy and single-molecule biophysics. Utilizing concepts from quantum entanglement, squeezed light, and non-linear optical processes, students will investigate how quantum correlations can surpass classical diffraction limits to achieve nanoscale spatial resolution. The curriculum bridges theoretical frameworks with practical applications in biological sensing, covering topics such as fluorescence correlation spectroscopy (FCS), stochastic optical reconstruction microscopy (STORM), and the analysis of single-molecule trajectories.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students will be able to design experimental setups for super-resolution imaging, analyze data from single-molecule experiments using statistical methods, and understand the quantum mechanical origins of high-precision sensing. The course aims to equip students with the skills to develop novel optical probes for biological systems and interpret complex biophysical phenomena at the molecular level.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 광학 기초 및 고전적 이미징의 한계 (회절 한계와 Abbe 한계)
2 주차: 양자 얽힘과 squeezed light 를 이용한 노이즈 감소 원리

4 주차: 초고분해능 현미경의 원리 (STED, PALM/STORM)

교과개요
This course explores the fundamental interactions between light and matter at the quantum level, bridging the gap between classical optics and quantum mechanics. We will investigate the quantization of electromagnetic fields, photon statistics, and coherent states to understand phenomena such as spontaneous emission, laser physics, and cavity quantum electrodynamics (CQED). Special emphasis is placed on semiconductor optical devices, including light-emitting diodes (LEDs), lasers, and photodetectors, analyzing their operation principles through the lens of band structure and carrier dynamics. The curriculum also covers emerging topics in quantum photonics, such as single-photon sources, entanglement generation, and integrated photonic circuits for quantum information processing.
교과목표
By the end of this course, students will be able to derive the master equation for light-matter interaction systems, design basic semiconductor optical devices using rate equations, and analyze quantum optical states relevant to modern photonics applications. Students will gain proficiency in simulating photonic structures and interpreting experimental data related to light emission and detection processes.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자광학의 기초 - 전자기장의 양자화와 광자의 통계적 성질
2 주차: 레이저 물리학 - 발진 조건, 모드 경쟁, 및 공진기 이론
3 주차: 반도체 광학 소자 - 밴드 구조, 직접/간접 천이, LED 및 레이저 다이오드 원리
4 주차: 캐비티 양자 전기역학 (CQED) - 원자-광자 상호작용 및 파동함수 붕괴

6 주차: 집적 광자 회로 및 나노포토닉스 - 웨이브가이드, 결합기, 및 칩 내 광 제어

교과개요
This course explores the intersection of photonics, semiconductor physics, and emerging quantum technologies. We will cover fundamental principles of silicon photonics for on-chip optical interconnects and LiDAR applications, followed by an introduction to photonic integrated circuits for AI accelerator architectures. The second half focuses on the physical mechanisms underlying quantum computing, including qubit manipulation via superconducting circuits or trapped ions, and the role of light-matter interaction in quantum sensing. Students will analyze trade-offs between classical optical systems and quantum advantages, examining how these technologies converge to solve complex computational and sensing problems.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design basic silicon photonic devices for LiDAR and data center interconnects, understand the architecture of photonic AI accelerators, and formulate physical models for quantum computing platforms. The course aims to foster interdisciplinary thinking by connecting semiconductor fabrication concepts with advanced optical engineering and quantum information theory.
학습윤리

강의실
소속
기초학부
교과개요
This course introduces the principles and applications of quantum simulation and computation using ultracold atoms as a physical platform. We will explore how neutral atom arrays trapped in optical lattices can emulate complex many-body Hamiltonians that are intractable for classical computers. The curriculum covers the preparation of degenerate Fermi gases and Bose-Einstein condensates, the engineering of tunable interactions via Feshbach resonances, and the implementation of quantum gates for universal computation. Students will analyze recent experimental breakthroughs in quantum error correction and variational quantum eigensolvers, bridging the gap between condensed matter theory and quantum information science.
교과목표
By the end of the course, students should be able to design protocols for simulating lattice models such as the Hubbard model using cold atom systems, formulate algorithms for basic quantum logic gates in neutral atom architectures, and critically evaluate the scalability and error sources in current quantum simulation experiments. The course also aims to foster interdisciplinary thinking by connecting concepts from statistical mechanics, quantum optics, and computer science.
주차별 강의계획
1 주차: 양자 시뮬레이션의 동기와 양자 우위성 (Quantum Advantage)
